```lua
local x = math.random()
```


You need to use Lua 5.2 or LuaJIT because [`%a` is not yet available in Lua 5.1](https://stackoverflow.com/a/51222710).

issue.body_normalized:
##### Issue type
 - Bug report

##### Minetest version
Minetest Server Version 0.4.17-1 compiled from source

##### OS / Hardware
Operating system: Raspbian Lite (Debian 9.6)
Machine: Raspberry Pi 2 / Raspberry Pi 3

##### Summary
Using `minetest.serialize` and `minetest.deserialize` on Raspberry Pi with long numbers (> 32 bits) truncates the number to a max 32 bit number.

##### Steps to reproduce
A good case is serializing a table storing a position hash. This is a simplified extract of code storing a position hash in an entity static data:
```
local pos = {...}
local staticdata = minetest.serialize({pos=minetest.hash_node_position(pos)})
...
local data = minetest.deserialize(staticdata)
```
Retrieved pos hash is not identical before and after.

Some more information can be found in the original issue involving position loss: https://github.com/pyrollo/display_modpack/issues/19

What I suspect is that the "%q" `string.format` flag is not working the same way on this system than on x64 systems.

Unfortunately I do not have any Rapberry and can not investigate further.
